title: Arranging Meetings and Talking About Frequency
summary: Making simple plans and talking about when or how often you do something.
whyItMatters: Making a plan requires more than naming an activity. You need to invite someone, ask when they are free, accept or reject a suggestion, offer an alternative, and confirm the final time and place.

mentalModel.title: Activity, time, confirmation
mentalModel.content: A complete plan answers three questions: What are you doing? When? Is the plan agreed?

mentalModel.title: Treat no as a bridge
mentalModel.content: When a time does not work, add an alternative immediately: 'Am Samstag kann ich nicht. Aber am Sonntag habe ich Zeit.'

mentalModel.title: Separate routine from appointment
mentalModel.content: Frequency words describe habits, while a day or clock time fixes one meeting: 'Ich spiele oft Tennis' versus 'Wir spielen am Freitag um sechs.'

ruleBlocks.title: Start with an activity or invitation
ruleBlocks.content: Use a direct question such as 'Gehen wir ins Kino?' or 'Möchtest du Tennis spielen?'

ruleBlocks.title: Ask when the other person is free
ruleBlocks.content: Use 'Wann kannst du?' or a specific proposal such as 'Kannst du am Freitagabend?'

ruleBlocks.title: Decline and offer another time
ruleBlocks.content: Combine a polite refusal with an alternative: 'Am Freitag kann ich leider nicht. Geht Samstag?'

ruleBlocks.title: Repeat the final details
ruleBlocks.content: Close by confirming the day, time, and place: 'Also Samstag um 18 Uhr vor dem Kino.'

tables.title: Conversation Toolkit
rows: Shall we go to the cinema?
Aber am Sonntag habe ich Zeit.
But I have time on Sunday.
Gut, dann bis Sonntag um drei.
Good, see you Sunday at three.

tables.title: Talking About Frequency
rows: Wir treffen uns oft am Wochenende.

patterns: Aber am + day + habe ich Zeit.
sentenceStructure: Open with an invitation or activity proposal.
Use a day, part of day, or clock time to make the proposal concrete.
Put the conjugated verb in position two when time begins a statement: 'Am Samstag kann ich.'
Repeat the agreed details at the end to prevent misunderstandings.

concepts: invite someone and ask about availability
accept, decline, and offer a simple alternative
give reasons and negotiate several options
discuss routines and availability with greater precision

comparisons.summary: The theme lesson supplies activities and frequency expressions for invitations and routine descriptions.
The modal lesson provides the sentence frame used to ask about and describe availability.

rows: Gehen wir am Samstag ins Kino?
Am Samstag kann ich leider nicht.

examples.de: A: Gehen wir am Freitag ins Kino? B: Ja, gern. Um wie viel Uhr?
examples.en: A: Shall we go to the cinema on Friday? B: Yes, gladly. At what time?

examples.de: A: Kannst du am Samstag? B: Leider nicht. Aber am Sonntag habe ich Zeit.
examples.en: A: Are you available on Saturday? B: Unfortunately not. But I have time on Sunday.

examples.de: A: Dann treffen wir uns am Sonntag um drei vor dem Café. B: Gut, bis Sonntag!
examples.en: A: Then we will meet on Sunday at three in front of the café. B: Good, see you Sunday!

examples.de: A: Wie oft spielst du Tennis? B: Zweimal pro Woche.
examples.en: A: How often do you play tennis? B: Twice a week.

examples.de: Wir treffen uns oft am Wochenende, aber nie am Morgen.
examples.en: We often meet at the weekend, but never in the morning.

commonMistakes.correct: Da kann ich leider nicht. Aber am Sonntag habe ich Zeit.
commonMistakes.reason: A brief reason or alternative keeps the planning conversation moving.

commonMistakes.correct: Wir treffen uns am Samstag um 15 Uhr.
commonMistakes.reason: Add a clock time when the plan needs to be actionable.
The conjugated verb remains in position two when a time expression comes first.

commonMistakes.wrong: End after several suggestions without repeating the result.
commonMistakes.correct: Also Sonntag um drei vor dem Café.
commonMistakes.reason: A final confirmation makes the agreed plan explicit.

specialCases: 'Wie wäre es ...?' is a useful fixed suggestion phrase before learners study the conditional form systematically.
'Möchtest du ...?' can be learned as an invitation chunk before the broader modal system is complete.
German commonly uses the 24-hour clock in schedules, while casual speech may use forms such as 'um drei'.
tips: Always practice invitations with one acceptance and one alternative response.
Use a real weekly calendar to answer availability questions.
End every role-play by repeating the final activity, day, time, and place.

memoryHooks.title: Invite, negotiate, agree, confirm
memoryHooks.content: Use these four steps as a checklist for every planning dialogue.

memoryHooks.title: No plus a new option
memoryHooks.content: Attach 'aber' and an alternative whenever the first suggestion does not work.
